recipient: East Africa (XEA); recipient organisation not named, recipient unspecified
title: Somaliland E-government Capability Enhancement Project
description: The Ministry of ICT of Somaliland unveiled the Somaliland e-Government Strategy 2020-2024 Action Plan, a government digitalization implementation guideline which requires many external resources for initiation. Government institutions in Somaliland currently work individually with limited information exchange. People have to visit multiple departments to take care of business and the service quality is unsatisfactory. Furthermore, data exchange among government institutions requires lengthy phone calls or communication. This system puts the overall operation under the risk of low efficiency, data mishandling, poor management, and tracking difficulties. As a result, cooperation among government institutions is challenging.This project echoes the 16th and 17th UN Sustainable Development Goals through establishment of channels for the government to be transparent and disperse information to the general public, while also enhancing the government digitization and e-governance capability. The main content of the project is to enhance Somalilands e-government capability through establishing a data exchange platform among government institutions, capacity building and institutional strengthening, and improving government network management.

title: Statistical support to Somalia phase II
description: Statistics Sweden has applied to Sida to initiate a second phase (2020 - 2022) of a statistical collaboration with the overall aim of strengthening the capacity of the statistical authorities in Somalia. Phase I ran between 2015 and 2019 and this second phase is now aiming at consolidating and developing the capacity and knowledge acquired by the participating Somali authorities in the first phase.This will be done by continuing to support the Somali statistical authorities. The overall objective of the project is thus to:Strengthen the statistical capacity in Somalia in order to facilitate decision-makers' awareness, understanding and confidence in statistical data.The project's expected results are:1) Improved quality in the production of social and economic statistics.2) Improved and strengthened capacity among the statistical authorities in the statistical method.3) Increased access to high quality statistics and data.4) Improved and strengthened planning and organization of the statistical authorities.This second phase is expected to strengthen the institutional and technical capacity of the Statistics Office of the Federal Government of Somalia (FGS) and of the Statistics Office of Puntland. Somaliland has been part of phase I of this effort and the ambition is to have them included again in this second phase.
